default._resident_note_1044:
**#1044 — the volume set's terrain shard: resident unmoved, and `ObjectStore` got 4 B *smaller*.** The set-upload session gained one field — `obc_app::SetUpload::terrain: bool`, the fact that decides whether the manifest this session will accept is `72 + 56 x N` or `72 + 56 x (N + 1)` — and the compile-time table moves **down**: `ble_object_store` 13,540 -> 13,536 and its `ble_total` 37,570 -> 37,566, the same 4 B seen twice.

The reason is a niche, and it is worth writing down because it is the opposite of what "added a field" predicts. `SetUpload` was `{ id: u16, shard_count: u8, committed: u32 }`: 8 B at align 4, with one **padding** byte and no invalid bit pattern anywhere, so `Option<SetUpload>` needed a separate discriminant word and cost 12. The new `bool` lands in that padding byte (the struct is still 8 B, measured) and a `bool` has 254 invalid values, so `Option<SetUpload>` now fits its own niche at **8 B**. `ObjectStore` holds exactly one, hence -4 B, counted once in `ble_object_store` and once in the `ble_total` that sums it. Nothing else in the table moved.

`.bss + .data` are unmoved at 295,808 B on the pinned host, `.uninit` at 118,432 B, the arena at 117,408 B, the poll frame at 9,728 B, the task body at 7,328 B and the residual stack at 77,280 B — the receive path adds no buffer of its own, and the manifest cross-check reuses `validate_committed_manifest`'s existing `#[inline(never)]` frame. `Armed` gained a `SetTerrain(TransferControl, Receiver)` variant, which is **narrower** than the `SetShard` variant that already set the enum's width, so neither `TRANSFER_ARM` moved. Flash is the `embedded` job's to re-pin as always: the pinned host links 1,357,880 B `default` and `ble` on this branch, against 1,355,528 B at the merge base — +2,352 B for the new object type, the `MS<id>.OBD` stream/commit path, the terrain record's commit-time cross-check and the session's clear-on-discard rule.

| symbol | Δ | what |
| :-- | --: | :-- |

A misaligned span still moves in 4-block batches rather than degrading to one command per block, and a one-shot `defmt::warn` reports the first one. |

| `.L_MergedGlobals` | +24 | the small statics LLVM merged — `flpr_mux::MODE`/`SEMMC_BUSY`, `ls021_flpr::SCAN_SEQ`, `semmc::COMPLETION`/`WARNED_NO_IRQ`, `sd::WARNED_BOUNCE`. |
| `flpr_mux::SEMMC` | +20 | the one `Semmc` host struct (clock/width/retries/counter/RCA/card), split per field by the linker. |
| `sd::SD_CARD` | **−32** | was `SdCard<ExclusiveDevice<Spim, NoCs, Delay>>`; `SemmcCard` is a ZST (the driver state moved to `flpr_mux`). The slot stays only because the `'static` borrow shape above it is what the extent fast path is built on. |
| embassy-nrf `SPIM00` instance state | −8 | the peripheral is gone. |

Symbols net +2,124; the sections moved +2,112, the 12 B difference being alignment padding the linker reclaimed. (The +2,134 / 22 B this note carried until the #1163 review round was an addition error in the prose, not a missing row: the seven rows above sum to +2,124, and the +2,112 section move is independently corroborated by resident 293,688 -> 295,800 and residual stack 79,400 -> 77,288.) `residual_stack` pays the same 2,112 B (79,400 → 77,288) because the bound is `_stack_start − __euninit`. `.uninit` and every arena figure are untouched — nothing here goes near the arena.

**The frames went the other way, and one of them was a caught regression.** `task_frame_measured` 6,912 → 7,328 and `boot_chain_measured_pinned_host` 28,116 → 25,700 (the SPI bring-up left the boot path). But the first cut of this PR made `sd::init` an `async fn`, because PR #1160 shipped `Semmc::start` as `async` — and awaiting that chain from `main` flattens its coroutine into `main`'s **task-body poll frame**, which is allocated in full on every poll forever: **6,912 → 13,376 B**, +6,464 B of permanent stack for a function that runs once at boot. This is the #677 / #1108 trap exactly, and `task_frame_limit` (8,192) is what caught it. `#[inline(never)]` does not fix it — it governs the future *constructor*, not the coroutine body (measured across four placements: 17,152 / 14,976 / 13,376 / 13,504). The fix is that bring-up is **synchronous** end to end: `Semmc::start` → `flpr_mux::bring_up_storage` → `sd::init`. Safe because the COM square wave the `async` shape was written to protect runs on the **P3 `InterruptExecutor`** (or, on `com-hw`, on TIMER + DPPI + GPIOTE) — it preempts thread mode rather than competing with it — and because bring-up runs before the ride loop, the BLE stack and the USB plane exist. It also makes PR #1160's "hold the mode across the entire `start().await`" contract structural: there is no yield left to hold across.

`boot_chain_ceiling` is deliberately **not** re-tightened from 29,696 to the new 25,700: it is a limit, not a record, and the drop is the SPI bring-up leaving rather than a budget being earned. `measured_flash` stays the `embedded` job's to re-pin, as always (the pinned host links 1,348,592 `default` / 1,348,584 `ble` on this branch).

**#1146 P3 the arena dividend goes to the frame caps: resident unmoved at 293,688 B, `.uninit` 93,344 → 118,432 B (+25,088).** The render arm *is* the arena's maximum, so this growth is the 1:1 half of the max-of-arms cliff — `MAX_SPANS` 1,152 → 1,792 (+8,960 B), `MAX_FRAME_POINTS` 4,768 → 6,208 (+11,520 B), `MAX_FRAME_RINGS` 1,024 → 1,792 (+3,072 B), `MAX_CROSSINGS` 256 → 640 (+1,536 B), and `size_of::<RenderScratch>()` (= `arena_render` = `arena_total`) 92,320 → 117,408 B to the byte, with no padding shift. `.bss + .data` does not move at all: the bytes are in `.uninit`, and the gate that catches them is `uninit_max`, exactly as P2 promised it would be. `residual_stack` pays the same 25,088 B (124,968 → 99,880 B), since the stack bound is `_stack_start - __euninit` and charges `.uninit` too; the deep-path peak it must clear is still the measured 35,808 / 37,760 B, so the floor keeps ~62 KB of margin. The other two arms did **not** change and did not need to: nav (59,872 B) and USB (16,384 B) simply gained headroom, now ~57.5 KB and ~101 KB of free growth before either would cost a byte.

**The net, stated the way #1146 frames it.** The three arms used to sum to 168,576 B of permanent residency (render 92,320 + nav 59,872 + USB 16,384 — 168,572 B as the five donor `.bss` statics, the 4 B being `NavArm`'s padding, per P2's note); the arena costs `max(arms)` = 117,408 B — **51,168 B less even after the +25 KB spend**. Measured end to end against pre-P2 develop the figure is 51,296 B: total RAM footprint (`.bss + .data + .uninit`) 463,416 → 412,120 B, and the residual main stack 48,584 → 99,880 B — the same number arriving from the other side. **Both figures are correct and they are not the same identity** — they differ by 128 B, and every byte of the 128 has a name: P2 already carried a 40 B gap between its own two accountings (76,256 by max-of-arms against 76,296 linked — the arena's 8-alignment in `.uninit` plus `.bss` repadding); #1150's review round put 8 B *into* `App`; and #1143's cleaning took 96 B *out* of it. The end-to-end figure charges all three, the arms sum charges none. 40 − 8 + 96 = 128. The arms figure is what the *design* buys; the end-to-end figure is what the *linker* delivered. They corroborate each other to within named linker padding, which is the useful claim, not that they are one number.

Measured on the pinned local host, whose merge-base build reproduces this branch's merge base exactly (293,688 / 93,344 / 124,968 on both profiles — P2's figures less #1143's −96 B of `App`). `measured_flash` is unchanged by the caps and stays the `embedded` job's to re-pin. Renders: only the saturating scenes move — `obc-bench`'s `overview` / `overview-rot` draw 1,024 → 1,792 of 3,625 features (2,601 → 1,833 dropped) and their frame hashes were re-blessed; `riding` / `mid` / `route` are byte-identical. The split between the four caps is this PR's review round's, not the original proposal's: the review proved that **rings**, not spans, set the feature ceiling (`select()` budgets points and rings and never counts spans, and every admitted feature is charged at least one ring), so the ring cap was raised to meet `MAX_SPANS` and the point cap trimmed by the same 1,536 B to keep the arm cost-neutral at 117,408 B.

default._resident_note_1146_p2: **#1146 P2 the scratch arena — one block, three arms: 462,392 → 293,776 B linked resident (−168,616), with `.uninit` 1,024 → 93,344 B (+92,320). Two futures shrank around the rewired locals: `__embassy_main::POOL` 33,088 → 33,040 (−48 — the `&'static mut` render scratch and the three nav handles that no longer travel into main's future; P1's +16 comes back with them) and `usb::run::POOL` 1,800 → 1,784 (−16 — `link::stage::Stage` losing its `&'static mut [u8]` for the scoped accessor `arena::with_usb_stage`). ble._boot_chain_note_1108: **Boot-path stack gates, added after the #1108 STKOF (schema v2).** Every image built from develop between #1084 (EL7) and #1108 hard-faulted at boot — a stack overflow at `link::init_store`'s prologue — and NOTHING in CI went red. The gap: `poll_frame_limit` only measures `TaskStorage<F>::poll` symbols, but the embassy **main task's** frame is allocated in the out-of-line `____embassy_main_task_inner_function::{{closure}}`, which that match excludes. EL7 inlined a ~2 KB terrain-parse temporary into it (20,352 -> 22,400 B) completely unseen. Three gates now cover it. `task_frame_limit` and `residual_stack_min` are EXACT measurements. `boot_chain_ceiling` is a deliberately CONSERVATIVE over-approximation: the walk follows every direct `bl` edge whether or not the path is feasible (a `Mode::ReadOnly` `open_file_in_dir` monomorphization still references `alloc_cluster`/`update_fat`, so FAT-write frames a rescan can never execute are counted) and is blind to indirect calls, so it is a drift detector, NOT a stack-safety proof — the on-glass high-water in ARCHITECTURE_RESOURCE_BASELINE.md is that. `boot_chain_headroom_min` is the invariant tying the other two together: ceiling and residual are independently re-approvable numbers, and #1084 failed precisely because three individually-reasonable changes summed past the stack, so the combination needs its own gate. Validated against the bricked image: on 5de00ce the same code reports task frame 22,400 B and headroom -7,932 B (chain 56,532 vs residual 48,600), versus 20,352 B and +7,044 B on the fix. **Host spread, measured on this PR's own CI run ([30852527404](https://github.com/timohueser/OpenBikeComputer/actions/runs/30852527404)).** `boot_chain_measured` is TOOLCHAIN-SENSITIVE in a way the resident figures are not: CI's floating stable links a 35,356 B ceiling where the pinned host links 41,556 B — 6.2 KB of inlining difference, since the walk's depth depends on which callees survive as separate symbols. `boot_chain_ceiling` 43,008 B therefore sits above BOTH so neither host false-fails, which does mean its sensitivity differs per host (~7.6 KB of slack on CI, ~1.4 KB locally). That is acceptable because the ceiling is the fuzzy drift detector, not the sharp gate: `task_frame_measured` reads exactly 20,352 B on CI *and* on the pinned host, so `task_frame_limit` — the gate that actually catches the #1084 class — is host-independent. Re-pin both figures from an `embedded` run, not a laptop.
ble._residual_stack_note_1158: **−20,480 B, and every byte of it is the sEMMC carve (epic #1158 PR1).** The microSD host is now Nordic's sEMMC soft peripheral running on the FLPR, and its firmware image needs a permanent RAM carve (storage reads happen mid-render, so it can NOT be a #1146 arena arm). `build.rs`'s contract places it directly below the display FLPR's carve: 17,408 B of image (15,360 code + 1,536 exec/data + 512 VRI) rounded up to the 4 KiB-aligned 20,480 B region at 0x2007_8000, so the M33's linked `RAM` goes 500 KiB → 480 KiB and `residual_stack` follows it exactly: 99,880 → 79,400 on **both** profiles, −20,480 to the byte. Nothing else moved — `.bss + .data` is unchanged at 293,688 and `.uninit` at 118,432 (the driver is dead code in this PR, so its own ~32 B of statics are not linked yet; expect a few dozen bytes when the integration PR wires it up). Boot-chain headroom against the unchanged 28,116 B chain is 51,284 B, an order of magnitude over the 4,096 B floor, and `main.rs`'s compile-time budget assert — which reads the same generated `M33_RAM_BYTES` — still clears with ~13.8 KB of margin. This is a **deliberate spend of #1146's ~51 KB net win**, which is what unblocked the carve in the first place; #1146 P3 had already spent ~25 KB of it on the render caps. The 2,560 B of slack inside the 20 KiB region is the price of keeping the image 4 KiB-aligned (the alignment every on-glass measurement was taken at) — see the `SEMMC_CARVE_BYTES` doc in build.rs.
